title: Military enlistment office medical board
what: Several doctors examine you at the military enlistment office and decide whether you are fit for service on health grounds.
why: When registering for military records, being called up, joining contract service or a military college.
duration: usually half a day or a day; the decision comes on the day of the board or later
tell_doctor: All illnesses and injuries - even old ones

prepare.title: Documents
prepare.text: Gather discharge summaries, reports and scans for all your illnesses. Without them it is hard for doctors to take an illness into account.

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Tests and a chest X-ray are often done in advance on a referral from the enlistment office. Ask there.

prepare.title: The day before
prepare.text: Get enough sleep and do not drink alcohol.

bring: Test results, if you were asked for them
steps: You come to the enlistment office at the set time
You see the doctors one by one: general doctor, surgeon, neurologist, psychiatrist, eye doctor, ENT, dentist and others
Your height, weight and blood pressure are measured and your vision is checked
If needed, you are sent for further tests
feel: It may take long and be tiring because of queues
after: You are told your fitness category
If you were sent for further tests, complete them on time
The decision can be appealed as the law allows

faq.q: What if I do not bring documents about my illness?
faq.a: The doctors may not take it into account. It is better to gather the summaries in advance.

faq.q: Can I have the tests with my own doctor?
faq.a: Further tests are usually done on a referral from the enlistment office. Ask there.

reminders.text: Military medical board tomorrow. Take your passport, summons and all medical documents.
